# PART 29 – THE MULTI-TRACK

[PART 29 – THE MULTI-TRACK] Contents of this Part

## Scope of this Part

[PART 29 – THE MULTI-TRACK > Scope of this Part] 29.1 This Part contains general provisions about management of cases allocated to the multi-track and applies only to cases allocated to that track.

[PART 29 – THE MULTI-TRACK > Scope of this Part] (Part 27 sets out the procedure for claims allocated to the small claims track)

[PART 29 – THE MULTI-TRACK > Scope of this Part] (Part 28 sets out the procedure for claims allocated to the fast track or intermediate track)

[PART 29 – THE MULTI-TRACK > Scope of this Part] (2) When drafting case management directions both the parties and the court should take as their starting point any relevant model directions and standard directions which can be found online at www.justice.gov.uk/courts/procedure-rules/civil and adapt them as appropriate to the circumstances of the particular case.

## Case management

## 29.2

[PART 29 – THE MULTI-TRACK > 29.2] (1) When it allocates a case to the multi-track, the court will –

[PART 29 – THE MULTI-TRACK > 29.2] (a) give directions for the management of the case and set a timetable for the steps to be taken between the giving of directions and the trial; or may

[PART 29 – THE MULTI-TRACK > 29.2] (b) fix –

[PART 29 – THE MULTI-TRACK > 29.2] (i) a case management conference; or

[PART 29 – THE MULTI-TRACK > 29.2] (ii) a pre-trial review,

[PART 29 – THE MULTI-TRACK > 29.2] or both, and give such other directions relating to the management of the case as it sees fit.

[PART 29 – THE MULTI-TRACK > 29.2] (1A) When giving directions, the court must consider whether to order or encourage the parties to engage in alternative dispute resolution.

[PART 29 – THE MULTI-TRACK > 29.2] (2) The court will fix the trial date or the period in which the trial is to take place as soon as practicable.

[PART 29 – THE MULTI-TRACK > 29.2] (3) When the court fixes the trial date or the trial period under paragraph (2), it will –

[PART 29 – THE MULTI-TRACK > 29.2] (a) give notice to the parties of the date or period; and

[PART 29 – THE MULTI-TRACK > 29.2] (b) specify the date by which the parties must file a pre-trial check list.

## Case management conference and pre-trial review

## 29.3

[PART 29 – THE MULTI-TRACK > 29.3] (1) The court may fix –

[PART 29 – THE MULTI-TRACK > 29.3] (a) a case management conference; or

[PART 29 – THE MULTI-TRACK > 29.3] (b) a pre-trial review, at any time after the claim has been allocated.

[PART 29 – THE MULTI-TRACK > 29.3] (2) If a party has a legal representative, a representative –

[PART 29 – THE MULTI-TRACK > 29.3] (a) familiar with the case; and

[PART 29 – THE MULTI-TRACK > 29.3] (b) with sufficient authority to deal with any issues that are likely to arise, must attend case management conferences and pre-trial reviews.

[PART 29 – THE MULTI-TRACK > 29.3] (Rule 3.1(2)(c) provides that the court may require a party to attend the court)

## Steps taken by the parties

[PART 29 – THE MULTI-TRACK > Steps taken by the parties] 29.4 The parties must endeavour to agree appropriate directions for the management of the proceedings and submit agreed directions, or their respective proposals to the court at least seven days before any case management conference. Where the court approves agreed directions, or issues its own directions, the parties will be so notified by the court and the case management conference will be vacated.

## Variation of case management timetable

## 29.5

[PART 29 – THE MULTI-TRACK > 29.5] (1) A party must apply to the court if he wishes to vary the date which the court has fixed for –

[PART 29 – THE MULTI-TRACK > 29.5] (a) a case management conference;

[PART 29 – THE MULTI-TRACK > 29.5] (b) a pre-trial review;

[PART 29 – THE MULTI-TRACK > 29.5] (c) the return of a pre-trial check list under rule 29.6;

[PART 29 – THE MULTI-TRACK > 29.5] (d) the trial; or

[PART 29 – THE MULTI-TRACK > 29.5] (e) the trial period.

[PART 29 – THE MULTI-TRACK > 29.5] (2) Any date set by the court or these Rules for doing any act may not be varied by the parties if the variation would make it necessary to vary any of the dates mentioned in paragraph (1).

[PART 29 – THE MULTI-TRACK > 29.5] (Rule 2.11 allows the parties to vary a date by written agreement except where the rules provide otherwise or the court orders otherwise)

## Pre-trial check list (listing questionnaire)

## 29.6

[PART 29 – THE MULTI-TRACK > 29.6] (1) The court will send the parties a pre-trial check list (listing questionnaire) for completion and return by the date specified in directions given under rule 29.2(3) unless it considers that the claim can proceed to trial without the need for a pre-trial check list.

[PART 29 – THE MULTI-TRACK > 29.6] (2) Each party must file the completed pre-trial check list by the date specified by the court.

[PART 29 – THE MULTI-TRACK > 29.6] (3) If no party files the completed pre-trial checklist by the date specified, the court will order that unless a completed pre-trial checklist is filed within 7 days from service of that order, the claim, defence and any counterclaim will be struck out without further order of the court.

[PART 29 – THE MULTI-TRACK > 29.6] (4) If –

[PART 29 – THE MULTI-TRACK > 29.6] (a) a party files a completed pre-trial checklist but another party does not;

[PART 29 – THE MULTI-TRACK > 29.6] (b) a party has failed to give all the information requested by the pre-trial checklist; or

[PART 29 – THE MULTI-TRACK > 29.6] (c) the court considers that a hearing is necessary to enable it to decide what directions to give in order to complete preparation of the case for trial,

[PART 29 – THE MULTI-TRACK > 29.6] the court may give such directions as it thinks appropriate.

## Pre-trial review

## 29.7 If, on receipt of the parties’ pre-trial check lists, the court decides –

[PART 29 – THE MULTI-TRACK > 29.7 If, on receipt of the parties’ pre-trial check lists, the court decides –] (a) to hold a pre-trial review; or

[PART 29 – THE MULTI-TRACK > 29.7 If, on receipt of the parties’ pre-trial check lists, the court decides –] (b) to cancel a pre-trial review which has already been fixed,

[PART 29 – THE MULTI-TRACK > 29.7 If, on receipt of the parties’ pre-trial check lists, the court decides –] it will serve notice of its decision at least 7 days before the date fixed for the hearing or, as the case may be, the cancelled hearing.

## Setting a trial timetable and confirming the trial date or week

## 29.8 As soon as practicable after –

[PART 29 – THE MULTI-TRACK > 29.8 As soon as practicable after –] (a) each party has filed a completed pre-trial check list;

[PART 29 – THE MULTI-TRACK > 29.8 As soon as practicable after –] (b) the court has held a listing hearing under rule 29.6(3); or

[PART 29 – THE MULTI-TRACK > 29.8 As soon as practicable after –] (c) the court has held a pre-trial review under rule 29.7,

[PART 29 – THE MULTI-TRACK > 29.8 As soon as practicable after –] the court will –

[PART 29 – THE MULTI-TRACK > 29.8 As soon as practicable after –] (i) set a timetable for the trial unless a timetable has already been fixed, or the court considers that it would be inappropriate to do so;

[PART 29 – THE MULTI-TRACK > 29.8 As soon as practicable after –] (ii) confirm the date for trial or the week within which the trial is to begin; and

[PART 29 – THE MULTI-TRACK > 29.8 As soon as practicable after –] (iii) notify the parties of the trial timetable (where one is fixed under this rule) and the date or trial period.

## Conduct of trial

[PART 29 – THE MULTI-TRACK > Conduct of trial] 29.9 Unless the trial judge otherwise directs, the trial will be conducted in accordance with any order previously made.
